notes: Two CATLOE teaching-center advice pages (design-and-write-AI-policies, addressing-dishonesty-and-ai); both coders marked both documents delegates. Matched units differed in 6 places: (1) actor/phase for two sample-policy permissions (student, during-work chosen because the sentence grants students AI use while working); (2) modality 'must' vs 'should' on 'each instructor will need to do this work' (should: advisory guidance, no rule); (3) should-not vs informs on 'AI is not a productive technology to use in the research process' (should-not, student, during-work); (4) may vs informs on the instructor-structured AI feedback line (may); (5) P66 vs P41 on the final 'value of doing their own writing' passage (P41); (6) unit_stance restrict vs neutral on the 'plenty of support' line (neutral) and neutral vs permit on 'students can and should negotiate' (permit). Only-A units (the 'more productive way to think about a course policy' principle, UNCOVERED, and 'If you lean into AI, you won't develop these skills', P41) were real policy text and kept. Only-B units: 'Your thinking and writing ... should be done by you' (P19, kept, modality should) and three practice-2/3 communication instructions (kept); 'they may decide it is safer to cheat than to risk a low grade' was dropped as general rationale with no AI content. The dishonesty page is about essay cheating generally, so its AI relevance is indirect.
